title: The Little Bird Behind the Waterfall
markdown:
The sun popped up over the big green hill. Bright! Sunlight poured into the meadow. Like warm honey. “Hooray!” Toffee the pony trotted out. Her hooves kicked up dew. It sparkled like tiny diamonds. Birds sang. Chirp! Chirp! The world felt bright. Bursting with new morning fun.

Rolo the raccoon opened his eyes. Sunbeams tickled his nose. “Morning, Toffee!” he yawned. Rolo loved mornings. But new things sometimes felt a little tricky. Like a new berry that looked too funny. “What will we find today?” he asked. His voice was soft.

Toffee bounced. She was so happy. “Anything! Everything! The sky is super blue today, Rolo! Perfect for exploring!”

A sound floated on the air. Soft. Like a whisper. Drip, drop, splash. That was the big waterfall. It tumbled and splashed. But Rolo heard something else. A sweet song. It wasn’t a bird. It was different. And it sounded a little sad.

“Did you hear that?” Toffee’s ears twitched. She heard everything.

Rolo listened hard. “Singing! It sounds like singing! Behind the waterfall!” His tail gave a quick wiggle. Behind the waterfall. A secret. A wonder.

“Let’s go see!” Toffee’s eyes sparkled. “It must be super exciting!”

“But the waterfall is very wet!” Rolo squeaked. Wet fur felt clammy. What if it was dark inside? He liked his cozy burrow. Safe.

“It’s just a little spray, Rolo!” Toffee nudged him. “Just a tiny bit! Come on! We’ll be super quick! And maybe someone needs our help!” Toffee had a big kind heart.

Rolo took a deep breath. Helping felt good. Like a warm hug. Toffee was right there. He nodded. He scurried after her. His heart thumped happily.

They ran to the big waterfall. Water crashed down. It sparkled. The air felt misty and cool. It smelled fresh. Like rain. Drip, drop, splash. The singing got louder. It was sweet. A little sad.

“Here we go, brave explorer!” Toffee stepped right behind the water.

Rolo peeked. It wasn’t dark. The water made bright rainbows everywhere. Wow. So many colours. Rolo stopped. He watched a rainbow slide down a wet stone and break into tiny sparkles on his paw. For a moment the crash of the water felt far away.

But the path was slippery. It jiggled.

“Whoa!” Rolo nearly fell. His paws slipped. He grabbed Toffee’s tail. His paws felt shaky. “Maybe we should go back, Toffee,” he whispered. “My burrow is dry and safe. This path feels wobbly. I wish I was in my moss bed.”

Toffee stopped. She saw Rolo was worried. His whiskers drooped. His paws trembled a little. “It’s okay, Rolo,” she said softly. “Just a few more steps. Look!”

And there, in a sunny spot, was the singing. A tiny bird. No bigger than Rolo’s paw. Her feathers were sky blue. But her wing drooped sadly. She sang. Tears rolled down her cheek. Tiny, like dewdrops.

“Oh, you poor little thing!” Toffee whispered. Her heart felt sad for the bird.

Rolo forgot the wobbly path. He crept closer. The bird looked up. Her eyes were sad. She chirped. “I can’t fly home,” she whispered. Her voice was tiny. “My wing is hurt. My family is waiting. I can’t get there.”

“Across the meadow?” Toffee asked. Her ears perked up. “That’s far for a little bird with a sore wing!”

The bird nodded. A tear fell. “It is getting late,” she chirped. She sounded worried. “And my tummy is rumbling. I’m so hungry.”

Toffee and Rolo looked at each other. They knew. They had to help. They couldn’t leave her sad and alone.

“Don’t worry!” Toffee said. Her voice was bright. “We’ll help you get home! We promise!”

Rolo looked around with his sharp eyes. He saw soft fluffy moss. Like a green blanket. “Toffee! Look!” he squeaked. “This moss is so soft! It will be a cozy bed for her!”

Toffee nudged the bird. “Can you hop on this, little one?” she asked. “We’ll make you comfy and safe.”

Rolo showed her where to put her feet. Toffee was calm and kind. The little bird hopped onto the moss. They made a soft nest. The bird snuggled down. Her sad song became a soft peep. She sipped water from a leaf.

“Thank you,” the bird chirped. Her voice was brighter. “My wing feels better.” She gave her mended wing a little flutter. “I think I can fly soon. Just a little more rest.”

Toffee and Rolo beamed. Rolo’s paws were no longer shaky on the wet stone.

The bird ruffled her blue feathers. The sun started to set. The sky turned pink and orange. The bird took a hop. She flapped her wing. She zoomed into the air. “Goodbye! Thank you!” she sang. She flew to her family. They chirped with happiness.

Toffee and Rolo watched her go. The waterfall splashed its song. The woods felt friendly. With a happy whinny, Toffee nudged Rolo.

“Come on! Let’s find more amazing things to do!”

Rolo’s tail went high. He scampered after her across the meadow, kicking up dew like tiny diamonds, ready for whatever came next.
